title: docker/docker-agent — AI Agent Builder and Runtime by Docker Engineering
content:
Build, run, and share AI agents with a declarative YAML config, rich tool ecosystem, and multi-agent orchestration.
docker-agent lets you create and run intelligent AI agents that collaborate to solve complex problems — no code required.
docker-agent is a docker CLI plugin and can be run with docker agent.
Define agents in YAML, give them tools, and let them work.
agents:
  root:
    model: openai/gpt-5-mini
    description: A helpful AI assistant
    instruction: |
      You are a knowledgeable assistant that helps users with various tasks.
      Be helpful, accurate, and concise in your responses.
    toolsets:
      - type: mcp
        ref: docker:duckduckgodocker agent run agent.yaml
- Multi-agent architecture — Create teams of specialized agents that delegate tasks automatically
- Rich tool ecosystem — Built-in tools + any MCP server (local, remote, or Docker-based)
- AI provider agnostic — OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Mistral, xAI, Docker Model Runner, and more
- YAML configuration — Declarative, versionable, shareable
- Advanced reasoning — Built-in think, todo, and memory tools
- RAG — Pluggable retrieval with BM25, embeddings, hybrid search, and reranking
- Package & share — Push agents to any OCI registry, pull and run them anywhere
Docker Desktop (4.63+) — docker-agent CLI plugin is pre-installed. Just run docker agent.
Homebrew — brew install docker-agent. Run docker-agent directly or symlink the binary to ~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-agent and run docker agent.
Binary releases — Download from GitHub Releases. Symlink the docker-agent binary to ~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-agent to be able to use docker agent, or use docker-agent directly.
Set at least one API key (or use Docker Model Runner for local models):
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...        # or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY, etc.
See Set Up a Model for the full walkthrough of both paths (cloud API key or local model).
# Run the default agent
docker agent run
# Run from an OCI registry
docker agent run myorg/agent:tag
# Generate a new agent interactively
docker agent new
# Run your own config
docker agent run agent.yaml
More examples in the examples/ directory.

docker agent run ./golang_developer.yaml
We collect anonymous usage data to improve the tool. See Telemetry.

report.summary: Docker released docker-agent, an AI agent builder/runtime as a CLI plugin using declarative YAML, MCP tools, and multi-agent orchestration.
report.background: Docker has long been the de facto standard for packaging and shipping applications, and now it's applying that same philosophy to AI agents. docker-agent is an official Docker Engineering project that extends the Docker CLI so users can define agents in versionable YAML files, wire them to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, AWS Bedrock, and Docker's own local Model Runner, and connect them to a rich set of tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It supports multi-agent collaboration, built-in reasoning tools, RAG pipelines, and even distribution through OCI registries — meaning agents can be pushed and pulled like container images. The move signals Docker's ambition to become the standard packaging and distribution layer for AI agents, making them as reproducible, shareable, and portable as containers. It also lowers the barrier to entry: no code is required to assemble capable agents, just YAML configuration and API keys.
key_points: Declarative YAML configuration: Agents are defined in simple YAML files that specify model, instructions, toolsets, and multi-agent relationships. This makes agent definitions versionable, reviewable, shareable, and easy to integrate into existing Git-based workflows, appealing to developers and DevOps teams.

Built on the Docker CLI: docker-agent is a plugin that runs via `docker agent`, and it's pre-installed with Docker Desktop 4.63+. This reduces friction for the millions of existing Docker users, letting them manage agents with the same command-line habits and infrastructure they already know.

Provider-agnostic with local model support: It supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Mistral, xAI, and more. Docker Model Runner also enables fully local, private inference, so users can run agents without sending data to third-party cloud APIs.

Multi-agent orchestration and rich tools: Users can create teams of specialized agents that delegate tasks automatically. Built-in tools include think, todo, memory, and a large set of built-ins, while any MCP server can be added — local, remote, or containerized via Docker.

Agents as OCI artifacts: Agents can be pushed to any OCI registry and pulled/run anywhere, just like container images. This enables a future where agents are distributed, versioned, and audited through the same supply-chain mechanisms used for containers.
report.impact: For the AI industry, docker-agent positions Docker as an infrastructure layer for agent deployment and sharing, potentially standardizing how agents are packaged and distributed through OCI registries rather than proprietary platforms. Developers gain a low-code path to build reproducible agents that fit naturally into existing Docker workflows, with provider flexibility and local model options that ease cost and privacy concerns. Regular users benefit indirectly: published agents can be run with a single `docker agent run` command, similar to pulling an image. The combination of MCP, modular tools, and multi-agent delegation also makes it easier to build complex automation without writing extensive application code. However, because the project is young, production readiness, security auditing of shared agents, and telemetry/privacy trade-offs will be important factors to watch before adopting it for sensitive workloads.
report.tools: Follow the docker-agent GitHub repository and its examples directory for official patterns. Docker Model Runner is good for local inference without cloud keys. For tool extension, explore MCP servers from the modelcontextprotocol/servers repo. Skim the OCI Distribution Spec to understand agent registry sharing, and watch Docker Desktop 4.63+ release notes for integrated updates.
